title: Shortest Path in DAG
problemStatement: Given a weighted Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) with n nodes (0…n-1) and a source src, find the shortest path distance from src to every node. Unreachable nodes should be reported as −1 (or ∞). Edges may have any real weights (including negative) — acyclicity is what makes one topo pass enough.
intuition: In a DAG every edge goes forward in topological order. If you process nodes in topo order and relax outgoing edges, when you reach u every predecessor of u is already finalized — so one pass gives correct single-source distances. No priority queue needed (unlike Dijkstra), and negatives are fine (unlike Dijkstra) because there are no cycles.

approaches.title: Brute: enumerate / Dijkstra-style without using DAG
approaches.idea: Ignore acyclicity and run a general shortest-path algorithm (e.g. Dijkstra if weights ≥ 0, or Bellman-Ford). Correct but slower / heavier than needed.
algorithm: Build adjacency list from weighted directed edges
approaches.time: O((n+m) log n) Dijkstra / O(nm) Bellman-Ford
limitations: Wastes the DAG property that gives a linear pass

approaches.title: Optimal: topological order + one relaxation pass
approaches.idea: Compute a topo order (Kahn or DFS). Set dist[src]=0, others ∞. For each u in topo order, relax all u→v. Because the graph is a DAG, each edge is considered after its start node is final.
algorithm: Build adjacency list of (v, w) and indegree[]
Kahn BFS → topo[] (or DFS finish-time reverse)
For u in topo: if dist[u] is finite, for each edge u→v (w): dist[v] = min(dist[v], dist[u]+w)
approaches.whyWorks: Topo order guarantees every incoming edge to v is relaxed only after its start is done; no later edge can invalidate dist[u] once u is processed.
limitations: Graph must be a DAG — a cycle makes topo incomplete / distances undefined under this method

python.notes: Kahn topo + single relax pass. Same as optimal approach above.

java.notes: edges[i] = {u, v, w}. Returns −1 for unreachable.

specialTechnique.title: When to use DAG shortest path
specialTechnique.body:
Use this when the graph is a DAG (dependency / scheduling / course-style edges).

Unweighted digraph → BFS
DAG (any weights) → topo + relax  ← this topic
Non-negative general → Dijkstra
Negatives / detect neg cycle → Bellman-Ford
All-pairs → Floyd-Warshall

whyWorks: A topological order linearizes the partial order of the DAG. Relaxing in that order is equivalent to dynamic programming on the DAG: dist[v] = min over edges u→v of dist[u]+w(u,v), with base dist[src]=0.
edgeCases: src unreachable from some nodes → those stay −1
Negative edge weights (still OK on a DAG)
Disconnected components with no path from src
commonMistakes: Running Dijkstra and forbidding negatives when the graph is a DAG
Relaxing in arbitrary order (wrong without a heap)
Forgetting to skip nodes with dist=∞ (still fine, but wasteful)
Assuming the graph is a DAG without verifying (cycle → broken topo)
patternRecognition: Sheet section: Shortest Path Algorithms after topo sort
followUps: Reconstruct one shortest path with parent[]?
Longest path in a DAG (flip min→max)?
interviewInsight: Say out loud: “Because it’s a DAG I can topo-sort and DP in one pass — O(n+m), negatives allowed.” That one sentence is the point of the problem.
